papers.title: The interaction of surface stiffness and hopping frequency on the metabolic cost and biomechanics of human hopping
papers.abstract: Metabolic cost reductions for stationary hopping on elastic compared with rigid surfaces are frequency dependent. We found that the surface stiffness that minimized metabolic cost was stiffer at faster hopping frequencies. Leg stiffness and contact time increased as surface stiffness decreased, and this effect was amplified at faster hopping frequencies. These findings suggest that the stiffness of passive-elastic devices, like elastic surfaces and footwear, should be tuned to movement frequency to minimize metabolic cost.
